# Experiential Labs: machine-readable reference

Experiential Labs is an OpenAI-compatible model gateway: one base URL in front
of every model, spanning hosted providers, your own provider keys (bring-your-own-key),
our platform-funded credits, and self-hosted or custom models, plus a public
model catalog, per-model provider waterfalls, organization API Keys, and usage
and credits. Use OpenAI clients for chat-capable models. Native decision models
such as TypeSafe Jev use their own API surface, documented below.
This file is the complete agent-facing reference. Human docs: https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/docs.
OpenAI-shared semantics: https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference

## Base URLs (local vs platform)

This deployment:
  API base URL: https://api.experientiallabs.ai
  Web app:      https://platform.experientiallabs.ai
This is the hosted platform. A self-hosted or local stack serves at its own
URL and its own copy of this file documents it.
OpenAI clients use base_url = "https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1". The management API is under https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api.
The /v1 base is canonical; the edge also accepts the un-prefixed paths a GUI
tool produces when it appends /models, /chat/completions, /responses,
/embeddings, /messages, /batches, or /files to a bare host (each aliases to its /v1 twin;
no other un-prefixed path is served).

## Authentication

- One header, always: Authorization: Bearer <key>. No X-Api-Key, no query param.
- Keys look like xpl_ + 40 lowercase hex chars and are scoped to ONE
  organization. The secret is shown once, at creation.
- Mint a key by signing in to https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/settings/api-keys; the plaintext appears
  exactly once. Key creation and revocation are web-session actions, not API-key
  actions.
- One key reaches BOTH the inference surface (/v1/*) and the management API an
  agent needs: catalog reads, custom-model and waterfall writes, BYOK provider
  connections, usage reads, and the org's key list. It CANNOT mint or revoke
  keys, change another key's limits, or reach platform-admin routes.
- Bad or missing key: 401 with {"error":{"code":"invalid_key",
  "type":"authentication_error"}}. The 401 does not distinguish absent,
  malformed, revoked, or expired.
- Verify a key works: GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1/models with the key -> 200 and the org's
  callable models.

## Two lanes (how a call is paid for)

- pass_through: your own provider key (BYOK). No markup: the provider bills you
  directly. Connect keys at https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/settings.
- platform_funded: our credits. Public-catalog models are priced from the launch
  catalog; each call draws down your credit balance. No markup.
Which lane a model uses is decided by its provider waterfall. Either way, the
gateway adds zero markup.
- Free tiers: some platform-funded models carry a promotional free daily tier
  (today gpt-6-astra and claude-fable-5.1). Eligibility: the org has a saved
  card AND one settled $1+ charge (adding a card alone is not a charge). Each
  tier has per-org daily and hourly token allowances (Astra: 500k input /
  100k output per UTC day and 200k / 40k per hour; Fable 5.1: 375k / 75k per
  day and 100k / 30k per hour); cached input tokens do not count. Past the
  allowance the request answers 429 insufficient_quota with a "free limit"
  message and does NOT spend credits -- unless the org opts into credits
  overflow, which bills the overage to credits at list price instead. That
  switch is ORG-WIDE (every free model). It is off for an org that has never
  paid and turns ON automatically at the first real payment (a Pro
  subscription, a credit top-up, or an auto-recharge). It can only be turned
  on by hand once the org has a card on file AND the settled $1 verification
  (the same bar the free tiers' card gate reads; a purchase or Pro satisfies
  it): an org admin flips it on any free model's page ("Past the free limit"
  -> Use credits), or an agent can
  POST https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/api/credits-overflow with Authorization: Bearer xpl_... (the web
  host, not the API host; idempotent). Without that, both answer 402
  verification_required ("add a card and complete the $1 verification to
  unlock credits overflow") and nothing changes -- so an unverified org's
  remedy is to verify, not to enable overflow. It can be turned off again from
  the same model-page row.
- "service_tier": "flex" (OpenAI's flex tier) on a Chat Completions or
  Responses request to gpt-5.6-sol is forwarded and billed at the flex rate
  (50% of base), at cost; on a model without tier pricing it answers 400
  unsupported_capability.

## Credits and subscription rollover

One credit is $0.01 of usage, not a fixed token count. Obtain credits through
Pro allowances, one-off top-ups, optional auto-recharge, and eligible verification,
onboarding, promotional or operator grants. Top-ups do not require a subscription.
Free replenishment and model promotional allowances are separate benefits.

Credits pay for platform-funded tokens at catalog rates, applicable platform-run
web search fees (default $0.007 per search on a finished host-funded attempt).
Ordinary Spend reports, filters and exports never spend credits.
BYOK provider spend is billed directly by the provider. Promo-funded usage is not
a wallet debit; a paid fallback or enabled credits overflow can draw credits.

Consumption order: soonest-expiring credits first; among non-expiring credits,
free grants/bonuses before purchased credits, then oldest grant first. Top-ups
and subscription allowances are both purchased credits. Rollover does not reorder
spending to prefer newer subscription credits over older protected funds.

Prospective subscription rollover policy: applies only after activation to eligible
grants from the effective date shown in the server-backed plan/checkout. Publishing
these docs does not activate it. While disabled, paid renewal adds the full allowance
without a rollover cap. Pre-activation subscription grants remain permanently
outside the capped pool, including pre-activation paid invoices delivered late.
Purchased top-up credits never expire and are excluded from subscription rollover
limits. Free grants, bonuses and model promotional allowances are unaffected.
The total wallet can exceed the subscription rollover ceiling.

- Monthly paid renewal: min(unused eligible credits + new allowance, 2 x new
  monthly allowance). A 2,000 allowance with 700 unused becomes 2,700; with
  3,000 unused it becomes 4,000, before protected funds.
- Annual: full annual allowance upfront. Same-or-higher annual renewal carries
  up to 15% of the PREVIOUS ANNUAL ALLOWANCE (not 15% of unused credits), then
  adds the full new annual allowance. At 24,000 old/new, 10,000 unused carries
  3,600, totaling 27,600; 2,000 unused totals 26,000. A lower annual renewal
  carries no governed annual credits.
- Limits run at paid renewal, not calendar month-end, a failed payment or a
  cancellation click. Cancellation retains the balance and stops future grants;
  re-subscribing does not grandfather governed credits. A scheduled monthly
  downgrade uses the new allowance at the next paid renewal, not when scheduled.
- A full-price upgrade preserves the balance and adds the paid new allotment.
  Rollover applies at the following natural renewal, not retroactively at upgrade.
  At a scheduled monthly-to-annual boundary, carry at most the outgoing monthly
  allowance plus the full annual grant. Annual-to-monthly has no governed annual
  carryover at the annual boundary; an unexpired annual grant never gets a monthly cap.
- A legitimately paid late older invoice is credited once but never caps newer
  grants with its older ceiling; its eligible remainder joins the next renewal.
  Payment restorations keep their original cohort and follow the same timing rule.
  This is not a continuously enforced wallet ceiling. Refund/dispute reconciliation
  accounts for prior rollover deductions, without double-removing the same credits;
  already-spent refunded credits may still be recovered.
Full explanation and examples: https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/docs/billing#subscription-rollover

## Models

- GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1/models lists the model slugs your key can call: the public
  catalog plus your organization's own custom and local models. Each id is a
  slug, e.g. "claude-opus-5", "gpt-5.5", "gemini-3.7-flash".
- A slug resolves through a provider waterfall: an ordered list of ways to reach
  the model (provider + provider model id). The gateway tries each rung in order,
  fails over on capacity and transport errors, and returns the first success.
  Organizations may override the default chain.
- Adding a provider key replaces the platform lane for that provider by
  default: with no custom order, your key takes the platform rung's position
  and the platform rung is not dialled. To use the key only as a fallback, put
  it below the platform rung in the model's Waterfall.
- A BYOK rung can carry per-key fallback rules: the failures the key is a
  fallback for. Set from the fallback-rules icon below the first rung. A key
  with rules never replaces the platform lane and is never dialled first, so it
  reaches a route only through a Waterfall that places it below another rung;
  a rule on a key no Waterfall places that way is refused (422) with that
  instruction, and on a model with no such chain the key is inert. An active
  restriction remains visible if the account moves first: reordering does not
  clear its account-wide rule or make it eligible for a first dial. Every
  failure is selected by default, so the key is a fallback wherever it sits;
  deselect to a subset (e.g. cybersecurity-policy refusals only) and its rungs
  are dialled only after a prior rung fails with one of those, never first. The
  rule is stored per account and applies on every model whose Waterfall places
  the key. An org can also connect several accounts for one provider, each
  under its own name (setup_alias).
- The full catalog with pricing, context window, and modalities is a public,
  keyless read: GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/models (no key returns the public rows; send your
  key to also see your org's own custom and local models). One model:
  GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/models/<slug>; its deployments: .../providers. Note the split:
  the /api/models* catalog reads are keyless, while GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1/models (the
  OpenAI-compatible list) requires your key.
- Data retention is browsable: each /api/models entry carries "retention"
  (zdr_all_rungs | zdr_enforceable | not_zdr | null when the model has no
  platform-funded routed lane), computed over the lanes the gateway actually
  routes for that model, and ?retention=zdr_all_rungs (or zdr_enforceable)
  filters the list. The model detail stamps each provider row with its
  "zero_data_retention" posture. GET /v1/models carries "data_policy" per
  model ({zdr, zdr_on_request, no_training, providers:[{provider, zdr,
  zdr_on_request, no_training}]}; zdr is true only when EVERY rung of the
  model's routing pool is zero-data-retention by default; zdr_on_request is
  true when at least one rung serves a require_zdr org, by default or under
  the gateway's per-request zero-retention constraint).
  GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/v1/endpoints/zdr (public, no key needed) lists every rung a
  require_zdr org is served through: model, provider, zdr, zdr_on_request
  (published only while the deployed gateway can dispatch the constrained
  route), no_training, routable, and the rung's declared capability
  flags. Browsing is not enforcement: the org policy
  require_zdr (a Pro feature; see "Zero data retention" below)
  makes the gateway route only through zero-retention lanes.

## Text embeddings

- POST https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1/embeddings is canonical; POST https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/v1/embeddings and
  POST https://api.experientiallabs.ai/embeddings relay to the same worker. Use Authorization: Bearer
  with your inference-enabled xpl_ key, and Content-Type: application/json.
- Check GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1/models with your key for actual availability. Intended
  launch models are direct OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, text-embedding-3-large,
  and text-embedding-ada-002; a model must be activated and available to your key.
  Read current input rates and model details from https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/models, not this file.
- Minimal body: {"model":"text-embedding-3-small","input":"A short document."}
  input accepts four forms: a nonempty string; a nonempty list of nonempty strings;
  a nonempty array of nonnegative integer token IDs (one vector); or a nonempty
  list of nonempty token-ID arrays (a batch). Empty strings or arrays, mixed text
  and token-array batches, negative IDs, booleans, and floats are rejected.
  Token IDs must match the chosen model's tokenizer. They are forwarded without
  decoding or automatic conversion between tokenizers. Upstream models enforce
  vocabulary and input limits; acceptance at the gateway does not guarantee
  token-array support for every custom provider.
- Optional dimensions is a positive integer supported by the model; omit it
  for the model's default. text-embedding-3 models support reduced dimensions;
  text-embedding-ada-002 does not. Input and batch limits are model-specific.
- Optional encoding_format is "float" or "base64". Raw HTTP defaults to float.
  The official OpenAI Python SDK requests base64 when encoding_format is omitted
  and decodes the vectors into floats. Explicit base64 leaves encoded strings.
- Optional user is a string of at most 1,024 characters, used for gateway-only
  attribution and NOT forwarded upstream. Unknown parameters are rejected.
  No streaming: omit stream or send stream:false for non-streaming compatibility
  only. stream:true is unsupported; all other stream values are invalid. Chat
  options, tools and prompt-cache controls do not apply.
- Response: object="list", model, data[] with object="embedding", index (the
  zero-based input position), embedding (floats or a base64 string), and usage.
  usage.prompt_tokens == usage.total_tokens. Billing is input-token-only using
  provider-reported usage; output tokens are zero internally. Vector length is
  not an output-token charge. BYOK is billed directly by your provider.
- NO embeddings response cache and NO Idempotency-Key replay. Repeated identical
  requests, including retries with the same header, go upstream again and can
  incur another charge. Completion prompt caching and internal router vector
  reuse are not endpoint response caching. Store vectors in your own application
  to avoid repeated work. A timeout may already represent billable provider work.
- Python setup: python -m pip install openai; export EXPLABS_API_KEY="xpl_..."
  with your actual key. Disable automatic retries if each attempt must be explicit:
    import os
    from openai import OpenAI
    client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1", api_key=os.environ["EXPLABS_API_KEY"], max_retries=0)
    result = client.embeddings.create(model="text-embedding-3-small", input=["A short document."], dimensions=256)
    print(result.data[0].embedding, result.usage.prompt_tokens)
- Token IDs with tiktoken: python -m pip install openai tiktoken. Use the same
  environment key. The flat array alternative input=token_batches[0] returns
  one vector; the nested arrays below return a batch:
    import os
    import tiktoken
    from openai import OpenAI
    model = "text-embedding-3-small"
    encoding = tiktoken.encoding_for_model(model)
    token_batches = [encoding.encode(text) for text in ["A short document.", "A second document."]]
    client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1", api_key=os.environ["EXPLABS_API_KEY"], max_retries=0)
    result = client.embeddings.create(model=model, input=token_batches)
    print([(item.index, len(item.embedding)) for item in result.data])
- LangChain setup: python -m pip install langchain-openai in your application.
  Use standard OpenAIEmbeddings with default length checking and tiktoken enabled.
  Its default path sends token-array batches for this OpenAI model; no custom
  client or tokenizer workaround is needed:
    import os
    from langchain_openai import OpenAIEmbeddings
    embeddings = OpenAIEmbeddings(model="text-embedding-3-small", base_url="https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1", api_key=os.environ["EXPLABS_API_KEY"], max_retries=0)
    vectors = embeddings.embed_documents(["A short document.", "A second document."])
    query_vector = embeddings.embed_query("What is semantic search?")
    print(len(vectors), len(vectors[0]), len(query_vector))
  LangChain may split long inputs and combine chunk vectors. Provider limits
  still apply per request. This setup does not establish compatibility with
  every custom provider or tokenizer.
- Errors use the common OpenAI envelope. Fix 400 invalid_parameter or
  unsupported_parameter using error.param; select an embedding-capable model
  for unsupported_capability. Follow the returned message for key, access,
  credit, rate, and provider failures; a retry has no deduplication guarantee.
- Embeddings do NOT run identity content-guardrail classifiers. A policy on the
  key's identity does not inspect, block, or redact embedding input or vectors.
  Validate sensitive input in your application before sending it. Content
  inspection is separate from storage and provider routing/retention policies:
  https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/docs/data-controls
- Guide and curl/SDK examples: https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/docs/embeddings
  OpenAI reference: https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/embeddings/methods/create
  Tokenizer: https://github.com/openai/tiktoken
  LangChain: https://reference.langchain.com/python/integrations/langchain_openai/OpenAIEmbeddings/

## TypeSafe Jev: native decisions for applications and coding agents

- Jev is a typed decision helper, NOT the primary chat model of Claude Code,
  Codex, or another coding agent. Keep the agent's conversational model unchanged.
- POST https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1/systemone with the SAME Experiential xpl_ key in Authorization:
  Bearer. Read the key from EXPERIENTIAL_API_KEY; never send it to api.typesafe.ai.
- Minimal body: {"model":"jev-latest","state":"All tests passed; a security review is still pending.","questions":{"ready":{"type":"noul","instructions":"Is this change ready to deploy without further review?"}}}
- Read answers.ready.noul as a probability, not a Boolean or permission to execute
  an action. Choice questions supply a criteria map; score questions supply an
  ordered criteria array. State may be text, an object, or an array. Questions
  are evaluated independently against the same state.
- Chat Completions, Responses, Messages, OpenAI tool calls, and streaming are NOT
  supported for Jev. A chat-family call is refused with unsupported_capability
  (Messages uses invalid_request_error); follow the /v1/systemone remedy.
- Provider-documented input context is approximately 32,000 tokens SHARED by
  state and all questions. It is not a total input-plus-output window. Total
  context_window, derived max_input_tokens, and max_output_tokens remain unknown
  in the catalog API. Do not treat null as unlimited.
- Gateway bounds, distinct from provider limits: 32 questions, 64 choice options,
  2 to 10 score criteria, 262,144 input JSON bytes, 64 nesting levels. No automatic
  retries or idempotency guarantee: a timeout may still represent provider work.
- Gateway examples and coding-agent prompt: https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/docs/integrate#typesafe.
  Official usage: https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/quickstart;
  input budget: https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives;
  agent skill: https://docs.typesafe.ai/agent-skill;
  launch: https://typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev.
  Upstream docs/skills assume a TypeSafe key and origin: explicitly override both
  for Experiential. The official skill does not make Jev a chat backend.

## Zero data retention (ZDR): what the platform keeps, and the toggle

Plain facts an agent can act on with only the org's xpl_ key (org_id from
GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/whoami). Full detail: https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/docs/data-controls; machine-readable
copy of this section plus the live provider matrix: https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/.well-known/ai-data-policy.json.
- The serving path is content-free: the request ledger keeps metadata only
  (request id, model, provider, tokens, cost, timestamps, status) and refuses
  prompt or response bodies by database constraint.
- The platform retains NO prompt or response content when the org switch
  "capture_prompt_content" is off. Off is the default for Pro organizations
  (the database turns it off the moment an org becomes Pro and deletes what
  was captured before); Free organizations default to on. While off, nothing
  is written for new requests and previous_response_id on /v1/responses cannot
  be resolved (resend the full conversation). Requests served on your own
  provider key never leave content on the platform on any plan. Requests routed
  under a ZDR requirement ("require_zdr", the account-wide switch, or a
  per-request provider.zdr) are never captured, even when capture is on, and
  keep no Responses conversation state either: such a request carrying
  previous_response_id is refused before dispatch with 400
  code=zdr_continuation_disabled (send the full conversation in "input"), unless
  the org opts in with PUT https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/orgs/<org_id>/provider-policy
  {"zdr_continuation_storage": true} (Pro, like require_zdr): the trade-off is
  that the platform then keeps that conversation state itself (30 days, under
  the capture switch); it is still never sent to a retaining provider.
  Uncensored models ("uncensored": true on GET /v1/models) are the opposite:
  requests to one are captured even with capture off (the usual size caps
  still apply), turning capture off leaves those captures in place,
  Experiential Labs keeps a copy after the organization or account is
  deleted, they are served only on Experiential-funded routes (never on your
  own provider key), none of their routes is ZDR, and a ZDR-routed request for
  one is refused before dispatch with 403 code=uncensored_requires_retention.
    GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/orgs/<org_id>/telemetry-settings
    PUT https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/orgs/<org_id>/telemetry-settings   {"capture_prompt_content": false}
  Turning it off needs Pro (or a grandfathered org): a Free org gets 403 with
  code "needs_subscription". Turning it on has no plan gate. Each flip is
  audited (telemetry.capture_disabled / telemetry.capture_enabled).
- Prompt caching (every plan): PUT
  https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/orgs/<org_id>/provider-policy {"prompt_caching": false} turns it
  off across providers. The gateway then adds no caching of its own (no
  cache-affinity key, no automatic Vertex AI cache, no cache-based placement)
  and drops cache_control markers and prompt_cache_key before dispatch, naming
  each in x-experiential-ignored-parameters. Providers that cache on their own
  may still do so: the header then carries
  prompt_caching->best_effort(provider_caches_implicitly).
- "require_zdr" is the org toggle that removes every non-zero-data-retention
  provider (and model family) from routing for the org, on every lane, BYOK
  included, before any request is sent; non-qualifying rungs are never tried,
  not even as fallback. An Experiential Cloud route that honors a per-request
  zero-retention constraint is KEPT and dispatched constrained: it serves from
  the upstream's published zero-retention list (last verified at the time on_request_listing.synced_at states on GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/v1/endpoints/zdr; older than 72 hours withdraws it) or refuses,
  and the upstream it selected is recorded on the attempt; natively
  zero-retention rungs are dialed first. A model with no qualifying rung is refused with 403,
  code model_not_granted, type permission_error, and a message naming the
  model, the toggle (require_zdr) and the providers that were excluded.
  Unknown providers count as not-ZDR (fail closed). "require_no_training" does
  the same on the no-training flag. Zero data retention is a Pro feature:
  turning require_zdr on (here, with the account-wide switch, or per request
  with provider.zdr) needs Pro or a grandfathered org, else 403 with code
  "needs_subscription" (the same gate as turning storage off); an org that
  already holds require_zdr keeps it. require_no_training needs no plan.
    GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/orgs/<org_id>/provider-policy
    PUT https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/orgs/<org_id>/provider-policy
        {"allowed_providers": null, "require_zdr": true, "require_no_training": false}
    DELETE https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/orgs/<org_id>/provider-policy
  Partial document: send only the fields you change, omitted fields keep their
  stored value; audited as provider_policy.set. Keep allowed_providers
  null: a provider allowlist is an Enterprise capability (403 "enterprise_required"
  otherwise). While the account-wide switch is on, lowering require_zdr or
  require_no_training is refused with 409 "zdr_switch_enforced" (turn the switch
  off first; allowlist and region edits pass). Takes effect on the gateway's next
  catalog refresh (seconds).
- ONE switch for the whole account: PUT https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/orgs/<org_id>/zero-data-retention
  {"enabled": true} sets all three facts in one audited action (storage off,
  require_zdr, require_no_training) in one database transaction; GET returns
  enabled (true only while all three hold), partial (turned on yet a fact no
  longer holds), enforced_at, the facts and models_with_zdr_route (judged
  through this org's own allowlist). It ENFORCES:
  a model with no zero-retention route is refused. The storage leg needs Pro
  (403 "needs_subscription" for a Free org; set the two routing toggles on
  their own instead); turning it off restores storage only for a non-Pro org.
- Three layers decide a request's retention: the platform (the switch above),
  the provider we send to (the matrix; an "Experiential Cloud" label takes the
  REAL host's posture; Experiential Cloud routes retain nothing and do not
  train when zero-data-retention routing is on, some routes may retain or
  train for plain requests, and zero-retention availability is last verified
  against the upstream's published list at the time GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/v1/endpoints/zdr
  states as on_request_listing.synced_at; a verification older than 72 hours
  withdraws zero data retention on request until the daily check succeeds
  again), and whoever is behind a router (a relay lane carries
  the upstream vendor's retention, so relay routes to closed-weights vendors
  and a constrained route's default routing are classed not-ZDR; a customer Modal
  deployment is ZDR only on Modal Server / Auto Endpoint / Inference
  surfaces). No zero-retention route anywhere today: claude-fable-5/5.1 and
  claude-mythos-5/5.1.
- Per request: a top-level "provider": {"zdr": true} (the OpenRouter-compatible field shape)
  on POST /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses or /v1/messages (extra_body)
  demands the same routing for that one request. Tightens only: no org policy
  is judged as require_zdr on; with a policy, require_zdr is forced on and an
  allowlist stays. Same filter as the toggle (native ZDR rungs, then the
  constrained route sent the per-request zero-retention constraint);
  x-gateway-zdr: true when served; 403 model_not_granted naming provider.zdr
  and the excluded providers when no rung qualifies. Other provider.* keys go
  verbatim to a constrained route on the OpenRouter-compatible Chat wire and are dropped elsewhere. Honored once
  the deployed engine pin declares the field; on an earlier pin every one of
  the three endpoints refuses the body before dispatch with 400 "The parameter
  'provider' is not supported by this gateway profile." (never silently
  ignored).
- The provider matrix the toggle is judged against (per provider, with
  per-model-family exceptions, from each provider's documented default API
  terms; re-attested at least every 30 days):
    GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/orgs/<org_id>/provider-data-controls
  Per model, GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1/models carries "data_policy"; every ZDR rung with
  its capability flags: GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/v1/endpoints/zdr (see Models above).
- Verify per response which provider served it: every completion response
  (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/messages, streaming or not) carries
  x-request-id, x-gateway-provider (the catalog provider of the rung that
  answered, e.g. bedrock, fireworks, azure_openai; a platform-hosted lane
  presented as Experiential Cloud reads experiential_cloud), x-gateway-zdr
  (true|false: that rung's own zero-data-retention verdict in the matrix, at
  provider + model-pattern granularity; a constrained route reads true exactly
  when it was dispatched under the constraint), x-gateway-route-depth and
  x-gateway-route-reason; non-streaming bodies (and
  the final usage frame of a stream) carry the same name as top-level
  "provider". After the fact: GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/v1/generation?id=<x-request-id>
  (provider_name) and GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/gateway/usage/events?org_id=<org_id>
  (provider, lane, attempt_count). Rungs removed by the policy never appear as
  attempts.
- Not attested: no signed tenant-wide ZDR certificate (x-gateway-zdr is the
  gateway's reading of the matrix, not a provider-signed statement), no
  data-region choice; a constrained route's zero retention is the upstream's own
  promise against its published zero-retention list, and Wafer's per-request header
  is not sent (its lane is classed not-ZDR). Vulnerability contact:
  https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/.well-known/security.txt.

## OpenAI-compatible inference API

GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1/models
  -> {"object": "list", "data": [{"id": "<slug>", "object": "model",
     "created": 0, "owned_by": "exp"}]}
  Scoped to the key's organization.

POST https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1/chat/completions
  Standard OpenAI Chat Completions. "model" MUST be a slug from /v1/models.
  "stream": true streams as SSE. Web search is served on every route:
  "web_search_options", OpenRouter's "plugins": [{"id": "web"}] and the
  ":online" model suffix all ask for it; a route with no native search runs
  ONE gateway web search (Exa) for the latest user turn, feeds the model the
  ranked results, and cites sources as url_citation annotations
  (choices[0].message.annotations; one delta.annotations chunk on a stream).
  Each gateway-run search is a flat per-search fee (default $0.007, never on
  BYOK) included in usage.cost; the count is
  usage.server_tool_use_details.web_search_requests. Only the "web" plugin
  id is served (other ids -> a named 400); without a search backend the turn
  still serves and the drop is disclosed (web_search->dropped(...)). Replayed history is served the way OpenAI
  serves it: "name" on role:"tool" messages is accepted and forwarded on
  OpenAI wires (dropped with disclosure elsewhere); tool and function
  "description" strings up to 65,536 chars (longer -> a named 400 stating the
  limit); tool call ids up to 65,536 chars, signed ids round-trip untouched;
  duplicate tool call ids inside one assistant turn -> a named 400 (fix the
  history). Plaintext "reasoning_content" is returned only on lanes whose
  operator declared the model exposes its reasoning (DeepSeek and Tencent
  hy4 lanes today); replaying it to any other route drops it with
  disclosure, never a 400. On a TOOL turn of a preserved-thinking lane the
  "reasoning_content" you receive is an opaque gateway carrier: replaying it
  verbatim on that same assistant turn keeps the model's thinking across the
  tool call, and stripping it is always safe. If your client edits that turn
  (renames or repairs a tool call, changes its arguments or text), the carrier
  is dropped with the
  messages.reasoning_content->dropped(assistant_turn_changed) disclosure and
  the request is served, never a 400. If the provider that issued it has
  since left the model's route, it is dropped the same way
  (messages.reasoning_content->dropped(issuing_route_unavailable)).
  Tool search is served on every route (engine 0.7.95+): declare OpenRouter's
  {"type": "openrouter:tool_search"} (optional "max_results", default 5) in
  "tools" and mark the rarely needed function tools "defer_loading": true.
  The gateway withholds the deferred definitions from the prompt, exposes ONE
  tool_search function, and when the model calls it runs a BM25 (or regex)
  search over the deferred tools' names, descriptions and parameter names,
  loads the matches, and re-dials the model on the same request. The caller
  sees only the final tool call; the search round is invisible and counts as
  one attempt; up to 3 search rounds per request by default. tool_choice
  "auto" and "required" work; a tool_choice object naming tool_search is not
  supported yet (experientiallabs/experiential#1047). With no deferred tool
  the declaration is dropped and disclosed
  (tool_search->dropped(no_deferred_tools)). Why: MCP-heavy clients with
  hundreds of tools spend 100k+ tokens per turn on tool definitions; tool
  search keeps only the relevant ones in context.

POST https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1/responses
  Standard OpenAI Responses. "stream": true streams as SSE. "previous_response_id"
  continues a prior response on any worker instance; continuations are retained
  for 30 days from the last turn, and only while the organization keeps prompt
  capture on. An unknown or expired id -> 400 code=previous_response_not_found:
  resend the full conversation. Under zero-data-retention routing (require_zdr,
  the account-wide switch, or provider.zdr) previous_response_id -> 400
  code=zdr_continuation_disabled unless the org opted in with
  zdr_continuation_storage (see "Zero data retention"). "store" is gateway retention: "store": false
  skips retention, so that response cannot be continued from; nothing is ever
  stored with the upstream provider either way. On native OpenAI routes the
  reasoning passthrough ships end to end: include=["reasoning.encrypted_content"]
  returns the encrypted reasoning carrier and accepts it back as input; a
  reasoning item replayed by id alone (no encrypted_content, the "store": true
  pattern) is carried verbatim for the provider to resolve; and
  "reasoning": {"summary": ...} is honored. An encrypted reasoning item is
  bound to the provider account that sealed it: replay one that another lane,
  account, or tool produced and the provider refuses it
  (invalid_encrypted_content). The gateway then re-dials the same lane once
  with the refused reasoning items stripped (your message, tool-call, and
  tool-result items are kept) and answers with the response header
  x-gateway-replay-repair: encrypted_reasoning_stripped; hidden reasoning
  continuity is lost for those items only. Keep replaying only the reasoning
  items this gateway returned to you. Non-function tool types in "tools"
  (custom, namespace, tool_search) are carried to the provider verbatim on
  native OpenAI routes. On any other route a custom (freeform) tool is served
  as a function with one string "input" (a declared grammar is stated in its
  description, not enforced; a route with a native OpenAI rung prefers it when
  a grammar is declared) and its calls come back as custom_tool_call items,
  disclosed in x-experiential-ignored-parameters as
  tools.custom->translated(custom_as_function_input) (plus
  tools.custom.format->translated(grammar_as_instructions) with a grammar); a
  namespace's tools are hoisted to functions and come back namespaced. Chat
  Completions accepts the same custom tools in its own spelling ({"type":
  "custom", "custom": {"name", "description", "format"}}, tool_choice
  {"type": "custom", "custom": {"name"}}, tool_calls of type "custom"), while {"type":
  "tool_search"} (OpenAI's hosted spelling) with "defer_loading": true
  function tools is run by the gateway itself exactly as on Chat Completions
  above: deferred definitions withheld, one tool_search function exposed,
  BM25/regex search, same-request re-dial, only the final tool call returned.
  The web_search tool (and
  web_search_preview, and the ":online" model suffix) is the exception: on a
  native OpenAI route the provider's search runs; on any other route the
  gateway runs one web search itself (Exa), cites sources as flat
  url_citation annotations on the output_text part (each announced by
  response.output_text.annotation.added), and reports the count and the flat
  per-search fee through usage.server_tool_use_details.web_search_requests
  and usage.cost. function_call
  "namespace" and SDK 3.0 "caller" attribution round-trip on native OpenAI
  routes and are dropped with disclosure elsewhere; function_call_output
  "output" may be a string or a list of input_text/input_image parts
  (input_file parts -> a named 400).
  The same path also serves a WebSocket transport: upgrade GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1/responses
  (wss) with the same Authorization header; frames cross unchanged and
  "previous_response_id" works the same. A deployment without the transport
  answers the upgrade 426 code=upgrade_required: POST over HTTP instead
  (the Codex client falls back on exactly this status).

POST https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1/messages
  Anthropic Messages API, translated onto the same chat surface and models.
  Auth: x-api-key OR Authorization: Bearer (same xpl_ key). "stream": true
  streams Anthropic SSE events. Extended thinking works on all-Anthropic
  routes: the thinking config passes through verbatim and thinking/
  redacted_thinking blocks round-trip with signatures intact. On a
  non-Anthropic reasoning route the thinking config translates to the route's
  nearest reasoning effort (disclosed as
  thinking->reasoning_effort:<tier>(<source>), where source is budget_tokens,
  lane_default for a bare {type:"enabled"} on a rung that pins a default
  effort, or gateway_default; an explicit output_config.effort wins and the
  thinking config is disclosed as superseded). budget_tokens must be below
  max_tokens (400 on thinking.budget_tokens otherwise, as on Anthropic). A
  request under 1,024 max_tokens with no reasoning signal of its own runs at
  reasoning_effort none on a default-reasoning route (disclosed as
  reasoning_effort->none(max_tokens_headroom)) so the reply has room for
  text. Usage objects carry Anthropic's four legs, including
  cache_read_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens from the provider's
  cache report. On a route with no reasoning the thinking config is
  dropped with disclosure. OpenRouter's reasoning object ({effort} or
  {max_tokens}, enabled) is accepted beside thinking and wins when both are
  present. A reasoning-exposed non-Anthropic rung returns the model's own
  reasoning as an unsigned thinking block (sealed in a trailing
  redacted_thinking block on tool turns) that replays on the next turn;
  Anthropic-signed thinking BLOCKS replayed onto a non-Anthropic route are
  dropped with the messages.thinking->dropped(unsupported_by_provider)
  disclosure, not a 400.
  Image blocks are served on every route whose model accepts images, up to
  100 per request; document (PDF) blocks need a document-capable route
  (otherwise a named 400 naming "messages"). tool_result.is_error=true is
  native on Anthropic rungs and folds into the result text on every other
  wire (disclosed), never a 400. max_tokens below OpenAI's 16-token floor
  rides the floor on OpenAI routes. Idempotency-Key is not honored here,
  /v1/messages/count_tokens answers an explicit 404 not_found_error (estimate
  locally), and errors use Anthropic's envelope
  {"type":"error","error":{"type","message"}} at the same statuses as below.
  Anthropic server tools: web_search tool types serve end to end on Anthropic
  routes (server_tool_use and web_search_tool_result blocks and
  citation-bearing text stream through intact and round-trip as history); on a
  route with a non-Anthropic rung the gateway runs the web search itself
  (Exa) and answers the same shape -- server_tool_use ({query}) and
  web_search_tool_result blocks ahead of the answer, the count on
  usage.server_tool_use.web_search_requests, a flat per-search fee (default
  $0.007, never on BYOK) in usage.cost. Without a search backend the turn
  still serves and the drop is disclosed (web_search->dropped(...)).
  Anthropic tool search: {"type": "tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119", "name":
  "tool_search"} (regex variant tool_search_tool_regex_20251119) with
  "defer_loading": true on the rarely needed tools passes through on an
  all-Anthropic route; on any other route the gateway runs the search itself
  (deferred definitions withheld, one tool_search function exposed, matches
  loaded and the model re-dialled on the same request, only the final tool
  call returned, up to 3 rounds). No deferred tool ->
  tool_search->dropped(no_deferred_tools).
  A bare thinking {type: enabled} is accepted (the rung's default effort on
  effort routes). Block cache_control markers are preserved on supported Anthropic
  and OpenRouter adapters and translated into Bedrock cache checkpoints. Unsupported
  generic adapters disclose markers as not_forwarded(provider_decides_caching; cache reads
  reported in usage.cache_read_input_tokens). Cache reads bill at the cached rate;
  authoritative per-turn usage is on message_delta
  (message_start carries the gateway's pre-dispatch estimate on
  non-Anthropic routes).
  Prompt caching is route-dependent: a listed cached price does not guarantee a hit.
  There is no universal organization caching switch or strict request-level cache-capable-route guarantee.
  Platform-funded one-hour cache markers are refused until duration-specific pricing exists;
  use the default five-minute markers. Verify cache reads/writes and ignored-parameter
  disclosures on your selected route. Chat usage.prompt_tokens_details exposes cached_tokens
  and observed cache_write_tokens; prompt_cache_key is an affinity hint, not cache activation.
  Block-level cache_control markers on system blocks,
  message text, and tool_result reach Anthropic routes verbatim, and usage
  reports cache_creation_input_tokens / cache_read_input_tokens with
  input_tokens excluding both, exactly like the provider.

- Reasoning effort ("reasoning_effort" on chat, "reasoning": {"effort": ...} on
  Responses, "output_config": {"effort": ...} on Messages) passes through when
  supported. If an effort is unsupported and the route's capability policy
  permits coercion, the gateway tries supported levels at or below the requested
  level, closest first, and uses only one compatible with the rest of the request.
  It never raises an explicit effort. If no such level is admissible, the request
  returns 400. Explicit "none" means reasoning off and can return 400 when the
  route cannot turn reasoning off; "minimal" still enables reasoning. A route
  supporting only minimal, low, medium, high cannot honor none: it is not
  upgraded to minimal. On a route with no reasoning support, an effort may be
  dropped only when policy permits and the rest of the request remains admissible.
  "max" is the top tier. Every substitution or drop is disclosed on OpenAI-shaped
  responses in a top-level "x-experiential-ignored-parameters" array; nothing is
  silently rewritten.
- Idempotency-Key is honored on Chat Completions and Responses, NOT embeddings:
  an exact retry on those completion routes with the same
  key replays the original result; the same key with a different body -> 409
  idempotency_conflict.
- Unserved /v1/* paths answer 404 code=not_found in the OpenAI error envelope.

## Error envelope (all /v1 routes; /v1/messages wraps the same statuses and
## meanings in Anthropic's envelope instead)

Errors are {"error": {"message", "type", "code", "param"?, "refusal_reason"?}}.
Stable codes (code -> HTTP status -> meaning -> recovery):
  invalid_json 400            body is not valid JSON -> fix the request.
  invalid_request 400         malformed request -> read message, fix, resend.
  invalid_parameter 400       a field is invalid ("param" names it) -> fix it.
  unsupported_capability 400  a whole capability the route does not expose (a
                              tool, a modality, reasoning) -> pick a capable
                              model; check supported_params and modalities in
                              /api/models.
  unsupported_parameter 400   a specific field the route rejects, e.g.
                              temperature on a reasoning-only route or top_k /
                              frequency_penalty / presence_penalty / top_logprobs
                              where unaccepted ("param" names it) -> remove the
                              field or pick a model that lists it.
  refusal 400                 the provider refused the request on policy
                              grounds. Message is always "provider refused the
                              request: <phrase>" (fixed phrase, never provider
                              prose) and the envelope adds refusal_reason, one
                              of cyber_policy | cbrn | content_policy |
                              recitation | data_inspection | unspecified, e.g.
                              {"error":{"message":"provider refused the request:
                              cybersecurity policy","type":"invalid_request_error",
                              "param":null,"code":"refusal","refusal_reason":
                              "cyber_policy"}}. Present on chat/completions,
                              responses, and messages refusals; absent on every
                              other error. Retrying does not help -> change the
                              request or pick another provider's model. Not a
                              key, credit, or limit problem.
  previous_response_not_found 400  previous_response_id is unknown or expired
                              -> resend the full conversation.
  zdr_continuation_disabled 400  previous_response_id on a request routed with
                              zero data retention: the platform keeps no
                              conversation state for it -> send the full
                              conversation in "input", or opt in with
                              PUT /api/orgs/<org_id>/provider-policy
                              {"zdr_continuation_storage": true}.
  invalid_key 401             missing/bad/expired/revoked key -> fix Authorization.
  uncensored_requires_retention 403  an uncensored model is only served with
                              prompt and response retention, and the org
                              (require_zdr) or the request (provider.zdr)
                              demanded zero data retention -> pick another
                              model.
  model_not_granted 403       your org cannot call this slug, or the slug is
                              misspelled -> use one from /v1/models. Slugs are
                              the dot form (claude-fable-5.1); Anthropic's
                              dashed wire ids (claude-fable-5-1) get this 403.
  idempotency_conflict 409    same Idempotency-Key, different body -> new key.
  idempotency_replay_unavailable 409/500  original keyed result gone after a
                              restart -> resend with a new Idempotency-Key.
  insufficient_quota 429      a spend limit, a free tier, or your credit
                              balance is exhausted; the message names which:
                              key_daily_cap (this key's daily cap; resets 00:00
                              UTC or raise it), a team/org budget,
                              insufficient_credits (add credits at
                              https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/credits), free_limit_reached (the free
                              tier's allowance is spent: wait for the reset or
                              enable credits overflow, see Two lanes),
                              free_tier_requires_payment (the free tier needs a
                              saved card AND a settled $1 charge),
                              model_requires_payment (the model or its lanes
                              need a completed top-up; the $1 verification
                              counts), model_requires_purchase (its lanes need
                              a real credit purchase; the $1 verification does
                              not count), promo_byok_only (the promotion does
                              not cover the full cost and the credit balance
                              cannot cover the rest: add credits or use BYOK).
                              Platform-funded lane only.
  org_under_review 429        the org is quarantined and cannot use models on
                              ANY lane (BYOK included) until the review is
                              lifted. The message says why in one low-detail
                              sentence: "too many of its requests were refused
                              by model providers for policy reasons" (a
                              refusals quarantine; adding credits does NOT lift
                              it), "for suspicious activity", "payment
                              verification did not complete", "the signup email
                              could not be delivered", or the generic "to fight
                              spam". Never counts or thresholds. -> reach us on
                              Discord or by email from the signed-in banner; an
                              operator reviews and releases. A settled payment
                              lifts every review except refusals, manual network
                              reviews and payment-review holds.
  unavailable_route 429/503   throttled or no healthy route right now -> retry
                              with backoff.
  gateway_overloaded 429      -> retry with backoff.
  request_cancelled 499       the client disconnected before completion.
  all_routes_failed 502       every provider in the waterfall failed -> retry;
                              if BYOK, check your provider key. Message
                              "provider stream failed" = the provider closed
                              the stream before completing (a provider-side
                              drop, not a gateway fault): retry with backoff.
  backend_unavailable 502     "Serving backend failed": the edge could not
                              reach a gateway worker (a rolling deploy or a
                              worker outage) -> retry with backoff; if it
                              persists for minutes, the gateway is down.
  provider_output_too_large 502  -> lower max output tokens.
  gateway_draining 503        instance is draining -> retry (hits another).
  deadline_exceeded 503       request ran past the deadline (no first byte in
                              90 s) -> retry after Retry-After (2 s) or shorten.
  internal_error 500          -> retry with backoff.
Retry 429 (throttled)/502/503/504 with backoff. Do NOT blindly retry
400/401/403/409: fix the request first. Retries can double-bill a provider
(at-least-once); Chat Completions and Responses honor Idempotency-Key for replay,
but embeddings do NOT. Repeating an embeddings request can incur another charge.

## Management API (same Bearer key; https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api)

Catalog reads (keyless-public: public rows without a key, plus your org's own
rows when you send your key):
  GET  /api/models[?modality=&category=&provider=&min_context=&sort=&limit=&offset=]
  GET  /api/models/<slug>
  GET  /api/models/<slug>/providers
Custom and local models and waterfalls (the key acts for its own org):
  POST /api/models                      create a custom model: {slug, display_name,
                                        providers:[{provider, provider_model_id,
                                        base_url?, ...}]}
  POST /api/models/<slug>/providers     add a deployment or local variant
  GET/PUT /api/models/<slug>/waterfall  read or replace the ordered chain
                                        ({model_provider_ids:[...]})
BYOK provider connections:
  GET  /api/orgs/<org_id>/provider-connections
  PUT  /api/orgs/<org_id>/provider-connections/<provider>       connect/rotate
                                        ({secret, config})
  POST /api/orgs/<org_id>/provider-connections/<provider>/check verify
Data controls (the key acts for its own org; see "Zero data retention"):
  GET  /api/orgs/<org_id>/provider-data-controls     the provider ZDR matrix
  GET/PUT/DELETE /api/orgs/<org_id>/provider-policy  require_zdr / require_no_training
  GET/PUT /api/orgs/<org_id>/telemetry-settings      capture_prompt_content
  GET/PUT /api/orgs/<org_id>/zero-data-retention     the account-wide switch ({"enabled": bool})
Usage and keys:
  GET  /api/gateway/usage/daily?org_id=&scope=&group_by=   rollup (day|model|member)
  GET  /api/gateway/usage/events?org_id=...                per-request stream (tokens incl. cached_input_tokens / reasoning_tokens; charged, estimated and free money)
  GET  /api/gateway/catalog?org_id=...                     aliases as your org
                                        resolves them, with each one's lane
  GET  /api/keys                                           the org's keys (never
                                        secrets)
Exact Spend reporting (provisioning xpl_ Bearer key, your organization only):
  Canonical base: https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/orgs/<org_id>/spend. The dashboard uses the same stores.
  POST /api/orgs/<org_id>/spend/analytics    {query,refresh:false,comparison?:"previous_elapsed"}
  GET  /api/orgs/<org_id>/spend/analytics/<id> resume the same load; optional comparison=previous_elapsed
  DELETE .../spend/analytics/<id>/comparison cancel optional work only (204)
  POST /api/orgs/<org_id>/spend/view         frozen query -> {report,series:{status:"ready",data}|{status:"unavailable",reason:"error"}}
  POST /api/orgs/<org_id>/spend/latest       {query} -> validated {build,report} or null
  POST /api/orgs/<org_id>/spend/snapshot     {query} -> server-frozen query
  POST /api/orgs/<org_id>/spend/builds       {query} -> free durable preparation
  GET  /api/orgs/<org_id>/spend/builds/<id>  status and committed progress
  GET  .../spend/builds/<id>/report          prepared totals/groups/buckets
  GET  .../spend/builds/<id>/series          prepared global leaders plus Other
  GET  .../spend/builds/<id>/export          prepared exact formula-safe CSV
  POST /api/orgs/<org_id>/spend/query        totals, calendar buckets, grouped rows
  POST /api/orgs/<org_id>/spend/facets       observed dimension/tag values
  POST /api/orgs/<org_id>/spend/series       selected-dimension stacks and spend leaders
  POST /api/orgs/<org_id>/spend/activity     exact filtered request/attempt detail
  POST /api/orgs/<org_id>/spend/export       complete snapshot as formula-safe CSV
  Get your org_id from GET /api/whoami. Every Spend route, including handles,
  requires a provisioning key: inference keys get403, foreign orgs404.
  Keys cannot impersonate a member with an actor header;
  scope=self requires a signed-in member. Backend members retain USER reads;
  browser routes retain their existing admin gate, not cookie-free key access.
  GET /api/v1/key is the presented key's own summary. Do not generalize that
  rule to all inference reads: existing Cost API activity and usage exports
  retain documented org scope (with separate plan-bound identity restrictions).
  Start with POST /analytics using an unpinned query, refresh:false, and optional
  comparison:"previous_elapsed". Loading returns {id,status:"loading",report:null,
  build:null,error_code:null}; retain id and poll GET /analytics/<id>, never POST
  again for an unknown outcome. Ready returns report with optional build; its id
  can be null on the fast path. Failed has error_code and no report.
  Server acquisition lasts60seconds from issuance; the dashboard observes for
  up to70seconds, not a longer server deadline or per-request HTTP timeout.
  Keep bounded poll counts and network timeouts. No Retry-After is promised.
  A known id resumes by GET; a lost POST response without an id needs explicit
  reconciliation, not an automatic new admission.
  Query example (replace dates with your desired UTC interval):
    {"start":"2026-09-01T00:00:00Z","end":"2026-09-08T00:00:00Z",
     "time_zone":"UTC","scope":"org","basis":"requests","group_by":"model",
     "filters":[],"tags":[{"key":"run","values":["eval-baseline"],"missing":false}]}
  Dimensions: model, app, key, member, end_user, provider, funding, surface,
  outcome, error, prompt, tag, source. app = calling agent (claude_code, codex,
  opencode, hermes, ...). group_by=tag also needs tag_key. filters entries: {dimension,values,missing,exclude?:true}; tags
  entries: {key,values,missing,exclude?:true}. Values OR within one predicate;
  predicates AND together. exclude=true negates that value/missing set, so All
  except selected values works across facet pages. No predicate means All;
  an empty included set means None. Omit exclude for ordinary inclusion.
  missing=true includes unlabeled usage in the set (excludes it in exclude mode).
  Ready analytics returns the frozen report.query: C=coverage.projected_through
  is Data through; F=query.as_of=coverage.as_of is the visibility fence. C can
  precede F. Reuse F and snapshot_id together across query/view/series/facets/
  Activity/export and matching build handles. /view requires a registered F.
  Page an ordinary table by POST /query with the frozen query and next_offset;
  stop at null. A regrouped table does NOT reuse a differently grouped build id.
  /latest is optional discovery only: without comparison it returns {build,report}
  or null; with comparison:"previous_elapsed" it returns a ready analytics
  envelope or null. Errors are not misses. Both latest and analytics reject
  supplied as_of/snapshot_id. An explicit refresh:true bypasses reuse; keep the
  same-slice complete result visible with its real update time while updating.
  /snapshot and /builds are explicit lower-level controls, not required before
  ordinary analytics. Timestamp-only interactive mode is not a registered fence.
  Expired or privacy-invalidated snapshots fail closed; explicitly refresh.
  Comparison is optional and never blocks primary figures: status pending/ready/
  unavailable, no totals until ready. previous_elapsed ends at query.start and
  has the duration from query.start to min(query.end,C), retaining primary C/F.
  Pass comparison=previous_elapsed on GET polls too. DELETE comparison preserves
  the primary. Never turn unavailable comparison into zero or a percentage.
  Series honors group_by/tag_key and ranks seven entities by
  spend plus exact Other, independently of table sorting. Missing and Other are
  distinct kinds; Other is never one model, prompt or tag value.
  Facets body: {query:<frozen query>,kind:"dimension",dimension:"model",search:""};
  tag discovery uses kind=tag_keys or tag_values with tag_key for values.
  Activity body: {query:<frozen query>,cursor:null,include_features:true}; follow
  next_cursor with the same query. source=intelligence entries are feature
  charges, not API calls (request_id=null, count=0); report links need member auth.
  Money fields paid_nano_usd/byok_nano_usd/free_nano_usd are decimal integer
  strings:1 USD=1,000,000,000 nano-USD. Spend=sum of those three. BYOK/free list
  values are not credit debits. Funding has platform_funded/pass_through lanes;
  promo/free is a money component, not a third exclusive lane. Cached tokens are
  a subset of input; cache read ratio=cached/input, not a request hit rate or a
  claim about savings. Reasoning tokens are a subset of output.
  Prompt groups identify repeated content without returning bodies. Signed-in
  members may inspect captured prompts via GET /api/orgs/<org_id>/usage/requests/
  <request_id>/prompt under existing capture/privacy/30-day retention controls;
  ordinary xpl_ keys cannot fetch these bodies. No capture/expired/erased =>404.
  Interactive bounds:50,000 source calls,100,000 fact versions per basis,
  368 series buckets,200 groups/page,10,000 CSV groups. On report_too_large or
  report_timeout with a snapshot_id, POST .../spend/builds {query}, then poll
  GET .../builds/<id>. Explicit refresh of a prepared result may POST an unpinned
  query to /builds: freeze/admission is atomic, concurrent identical refreshes
  within5seconds join active work, and the response retains the actual cutoff.
  Once completed, read /report (sort,direction,offset,limit), /series or /export
  from that build. Preparation is free; no partial totals or inference call.
  Builds expire after24h and retain at most10,000 groups,100,000 cells,32MiB
  logical output (CSV16MiB). Capacity/output/expiry failures are explicit.
  Rollout is opt-in: no snapshot_id means preparation is not enabled; retain
  the interactive limit and narrow dates. Monthly only solves bucket limits.
  Facets/Activity keep interactive limits even after an aggregate is prepared.
  Incomplete exports return409; do not treat unknown usage as zero.
  SpendFigures has exactly11 fields: count,rejected_count,errors,input_tokens,
  output_tokens,cached_input_tokens,reasoning_tokens,paid_nano_usd,byok_nano_usd,
  free_nano_usd,unknown_usage_count. No serialized spend_nano_usd on report figures;
  derive the three-leg sum with integer arithmetic. errors=non-completed outcomes,
  rejected_count is its failed/expired zero-attempt subset, never additive.
  Unknown usage makes measured money provisional even under complete coverage.
  Protocol rejections before admission are not included; pending holds are not Spend.
  Lightweight summaries: GET /api/orgs/<org_id>/usage/by-key and /usage/by-identity
  require provisioning strength too. window=24h|7d|30d(default7d). Envelopes carry
  report_kind:"live_usage_summary", window, and keys or identities. Model rows
  and key/identity totals retain cost_usd/estimated_cost_usd/free_usd plus exact
  decimal strings paid_nano_usd/byok_nano_usd/free_nano_usd/spend_nano_usd.
  spend_nano_usd=paid+byok+free, not all charged. One consistent bounded rollup read,
  max10,000 key/model cells (not keys),32 MiB source-cell JSON budget; final response
  formatting has separate overhead. Transport overhead can reach the source-read
  bound earlier. No offset stitching or partial success.
  Oversize returns422 code usage_summary_too_large, use Spend analytics.
  These are live summaries, not certified coverage: unknown usage is not reported,
  not zero. Never synthesize complete:true or unknown_usage_count:0.
  Full contracts and bounded curl/Python examples: https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/docs/spend-api.
  Dashboard guide and request tags: https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/docs/spend.
  Request tags are API-first: send key/value labels on each inference request,
  not a separate dashboard creation step. Send X-Explabs-Tags:
  {"team":"search","run":"eval-September"}. Python SDK calls use
  extra_headers={"X-Explabs-Tags": json.dumps(tags)}.
  Supported HTTP POST routes: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/messages.
  The gateway collects tags for Spend and strips the header before forwarding to providers.
  Batch tags and WebSocket tags are not supported; unsupported routes refuse the header.
  New keys/values are discovered automatically after tagged calls settle and usage
  updates; no pre-registration or dashboard definition is required.
  In Spend, Views -> Tag -> team groups teams; Filters -> Tag -> team -> search
  narrows to that value. Multiple values use OR, separate tag keys use AND.
  Limits: <=16 entries,8 KiB. Never send secrets, prompts or personal data.
  Workspace admins may optionally save advisory definitions in the Tags UI.
  Create tag only saves a suggested pair and copyable header, not request usage;
  it does not enable collection. Accepted request tags are immutable attribution;
  later definitions or retries cannot rewrite them. Older untagged calls stay untagged.
  Member-authenticated catalogue: GET/POST /api/orgs/<org_id>/spend/tag-definitions
  ({tag_key,tag_value} for POST), GET .../tag-definitions/keys, and DELETE
  .../tag-definitions/<definition_id>. Exact pairs are idempotent; max1,000 per
  workspace, pages<=200. Only actual admin members write; xpl_ inference keys
  cannot use this management door. Definitions do not rewrite past requests,
  confer permissions, or constrain valid observed tags; deletion preserves
  observed history. UI marks catalogue entries Defined, not proof of usage.
  Spend Views select a breakdown independently of Filters. Filters(n) reveals
  removable pills and immediately opens the picker; edits never change the view.
  Pinned chart rows open a separate funding popup without resizing the bucket.
  Spend requires workspace-admin or platform-admin access. Usage intelligence
  on the Spend page is internal to Experiential (platform admins only) and is
  not a customer API. Returning to a loaded report
  preserves its frozen results, rows, scroll and draft without a full reload;
  explicit refresh still loads a new snapshot. Evals is a separate sidebar
  page at /evals, preserving the existing platform-admin-only prototype.
  Spend UI rounds dollars to two decimals (<$0.01 below display precision);
  API and CSV retain exact integer nano-USD/nine-decimal USD respectively.
Archived Projects:
  The trace-backed optimizer, router-building, and Project-serving surfaces are
  retained for historical data and operator recovery only. Their UI routes are
  closed and no API key reaches their routes; do not use them as an inference
  API or as an alternate modeling implementation.
Trace telemetry (bring your traces in as telemetry only; never a router build;
the key acts for its org):
  POST /api/orgs/<org_id>/telemetry/traces/pull   live pull from a provider:
                                        {transport_kind, source_kind,
                                        source_label, credential, config?}.
                                        transport_kind is one of: braintrust,
                                        langsmith, langfuse, posthog, mastra,
                                        postgres. The credential is used once and
                                        never stored on the row.
  POST /api/orgs/<org_id>/telemetry/traces/upload  JSON {source_kind,
                                        source_label} returns a short-lived
                                        signed Storage URL/token (PUT exact raw
                                        bytes; 2h; path-bound; no overwrite).
  POST /api/orgs/<org_id>/telemetry/traces/<ingest_id>/finalize
                                        idempotent 202 accepted; the worker
                                        verifies the object then projects.
                                        Same formats and <=50MB as before.
                                        Arize/Phoenix have no live pull yet, use
                                        this with source_kind phoenix (or otlp).
  GET  /api/orgs/<org_id>/telemetry/traces   the org's landed telemetry traces
                                        plus total_ingests and total_traces (the
                                        verify-count). Humans see these at
                                        https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/telemetry. This path never creates
                                        a Project, preparation, or optimize job.
Live export to Langfuse (OpenTelemetry; an org admin turns it on once in
Settings > Connections > Langfuse > Live export, details at https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/docs/telemetry#export):
  Every /v1 chat, Responses, Messages and embeddings call becomes one span in
  the org's Langfuse project with input/output, usage, cost, time to first
  token and errors, streaming included. Send the W3C traceparent header of
  your active span to nest the call under your app's trace. Optional headers:
  X-Explabs-Trace-Name, X-Explabs-Session-Id, X-Explabs-User-Id,
  X-Explabs-Observation-Name; X-Explabs-Tags become observation metadata.
  ZDR-routed requests export metadata only. Best effort; never affects calls.
  Covers accepted HTTP calls; pre-admission refusals and Responses over
  WebSocket are not exported.
  GET/PUT/DELETE https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/orgs/<org_id>/observation-export   with the org's own
    key: {"enabled": true, "include_content": true, "langfuse": {"public_key":
    "pk-lf-...", "secret_key": "sk-lf-...", "host": "https://us.cloud.langfuse.com"}}
    connects or rotates Langfuse and turns export on in one call; omit
    "langfuse" to toggle an existing connection. Keys are never returned.
Providers accepted on a deployment: openai, anthropic, gemini, azure_openai,
openrouter, bedrock, local, fireworks, modal, zai, qwen, tencent, vertex,
meta, cerebras, wafer, huawei, experiential_cloud.
Experiential Cloud is a curated collection of models, hosted and optimized by
Experiential Labs. Call it with an xpl_ key. Organizations do not connect
their own credentials to it. BYOK connections: openai, anthropic, gemini,
azure_openai, openrouter, bedrock, fireworks, modal, vertex, zai, qwen,
tencent, meta, cerebras, wafer, huawei.

## Integration API: compatible routes, cost, and account (https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/v1)

One base URL, https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/v1, serves inference, model discovery, cost, and key
management with one xpl_ key. Coming from another gateway such as OpenRouter:
point base_url at https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/v1 and keep working; the path shapes match.
Switching a project from OpenRouter: the "Switch from OpenRouter" prompt under
"Setup prompts" below is the complete one-paste transfer (base URL and key
swap, model-id mapping against GET /api/v1/models, the OpenRouter-only fields
to remove, cost reads, one verified call, BYOK offer); nothing else needs
reading. OpenRouter-style model ids are accepted at request time only as
spellings of a catalog slug: <vendor>/<slug> when the vendor names the
model's maker (or one of its OpenRouter listings) and the part after the
slash IS the slug, and <slug>:free for a model with a free lane; <slug>:online
asks for web search (served on every route, per-search fee); :nitro, :floor,
:thinking and the other OpenRouter suffixes are not spellings and deny like an
unknown model. Prefer the plain slug.
Human docs: https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/docs/integrate (paste-able integration prompts + route map),
https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/docs/cost-api (cost, usage export, attribution, metering), and
https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/docs/account-api (keys). The two generic integration prompts and both
provider-specific transfers are also under "Setup prompts" below.
For Cloudflare AI Gateway, use "Switch from Cloudflare AI Gateway" at
https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/docs/setup-prompts#switch-from-cloudflare-ai-gateway.
It inventories rules, trusted customer identities, model groups and allowances,
reset/carry-in semantics, cost basis, BYOK/custom providers, privacy, cache and
retry behavior before proposing changes. Existing Account/Cost APIs are not proof
of customer-plan parity: discover native policy APIs in this deployment's live
docs, verify their deployment and test the actual workflow. External subscription
events, polling settled exports and invoicing remain application integration.
Wallet charges and attributed BYOK estimates are distinct. Tinfoil attestation
needs separate proof; Modal stays separate. Ask before writes, spend, privacy
changes, cutover or secret revocation. Stop before cutover on unsupported
requirements or absent live verification; never assume full Cloudflare parity.

Custom endpoints: https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/docs/integrate#custom-endpoints documents the exact
model-bound create/check and optional rate_card contract. Both custom endpoint
POSTs need a unique explicit setup_alias. Creation is create-only (409 on an
existing name); tests and creation probes may incur provider charges. Rates
are integer nano-USD per million tokens, never extra auth/provider config.
Missing custom rates are unknown, not public-provider rates and not zero.
Attempts freeze the selected full schedule, pricing_source digest and effective
date. To change a custom key or card, create a new custom account then explicitly
select Use on the model; generic provider PUT/check refuses custom accounts
before an official-provider probe. Preserve the old account for rollback.

Serving and discovery (1:1 relay to the gateway worker; OpenAI / Anthropic wire
formats unchanged): POST /api/v1/chat/completions, POST /api/v1/responses (HTTP
or WebSocket upgrade), POST /api/v1/embeddings (text or token IDs, no streaming or replay),
POST /api/v1/messages (Anthropic Messages API). GET /api/v1/models lists the same
callable set as /v1/models in the vendor-prefixed id shape.
The POST routes are rewritten to their /v1 twins before auth, so https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/v1 behaves
exactly like https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1 for them.
Catalog (control plane): GET /api/v1/models/{author}/{slug}/endpoints (per-model
provider waterfall; {author} is accepted but resolution is by {slug}), GET
/api/v1/providers. Metadata we do not track is null or omitted, never faked.

Cost API (read-only; an ordinary inference key):
- Inline: usage.cost (USD, what was charged) is stamped on every Chat/Responses/
  Messages reply, on the final usage chunk when streaming (message_delta on
  Messages), no flag needed (usage.include
  and stream_options.include_usage are accepted no-ops). BYOK settles cost 0
  with usage.is_byok true and usage.cost_details.upstream_inference_cost. The
  top-level provider field names the rung that actually served (tencent,
  fireworks, ...), since a waterfall can fail over silently; a lane the
  platform presents as its own reads experiential_cloud there and in every
  catalog and usage view (same field, same routing and prices). A
  request sent with Idempotency-Key carries NO usage.cost on the original or a
  replay (bytes stay identical): treat the field as optional; the export row
  still exists.
- One request: the completion response carries an x-request-id header (the
  gateway request id); GET /api/v1/generation?id=<id> (bare or gen-<id>)
  returns {data:{total_cost, provider_name, tokens...}}. Org-scoped: another
  org's id 404s like an unknown one.
- Balance: GET /api/v1/credits -> {data:{total_credits, total_usage}} in USD;
  balance = total_credits - total_usage. Recent rollup: GET /api/v1/activity.
- Presented key: GET /api/v1/key -> usage/limit/limit_remaining for the key
  making the call (limit is a daily USD cap; needs an xpl_ credential, a
  browser session 400s).
- Settled export: GET /api/v1/usage?limit=1000 -> {data:[row...],
  next_cursor:{cursor_ts,cursor_id,cursor_after}|null}, newest first; pass the
  three cursor values back as query params for the next page; filters
  attribution_label, model, api_key_id, status, window. Row fields: id,
  created_at, model, provider, attribution_label, real_cost_usd (= cost_usd +
  estimated_cost_usd; 0 with pricing_known false means unpriced, not free),
  cost_usd (charged credits only), estimated_cost_usd (attributed BYOK value at
  catalog list rates: an estimate, never the provider's invoice),
  pricing_known, input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_input_tokens,
  reasoning_tokens, status, api_key_id. Rows never change once settled. Pull /
  poll; no webhook.
- Attribution: send the end-customer's stable id as safety_identifier (alias:
  user) on every request; it comes back as attribution_label.
- Metering pattern (consumption credits via Metronome / Orb / Stripe meters):
  tag requests with safety_identifier. next_cursor pages OLDER within one call's
  window (24h|7d|30d, default 7d); it is NOT a cross-run checkpoint. Each
  scheduled run starts at the top of GET /api/v1/usage?limit=1000, follows
  next_cursor until a whole page is older than the last successful run's start
  minus a grace period, and dedupes on row id; run at least daily (rows older
  than 30d are not exportable). Land rows in a local outbox keyed on row id in
  one transaction, then a separate delivery step pushes unsent rows: one usage
  event per row with transaction_id/idempotency key = row id, timestamp =
  created_at, quantity = real_cost_usd (or cost_usd plus tokens for BYOK rows,
  since estimated_cost_usd is a catalog-rate estimate, never the provider's
  invoice). Price the margin in the billing system, not the sync. Reconcile the
  export's cost_usd column (charged credits only) summed per day against the
  movement of /credits total_usage. Bill from the export, never from the inline
  usage.cost.

Account API:
- One xpl_ key type. A normal key is an INFERENCE key: inference plus every
  read above. A PROVISIONING key is the same xpl_ key minted with
  "provisioning": true (api_keys.is_provisioning); the whole /api/v1/keys*
  family (GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE, reads included) is gated behind it and a
  normal key gets 403. The FIRST provisioning key is minted from the dashboard
  at https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/api-keys (a signed-in org admin satisfies the same gate);
  thereafter a provisioning key mints more via POST /api/v1/keys. Keep it
  server-side; never use it for inference traffic.
- GET /api/v1/keys (revoked hidden unless ?include_disabled=true); POST
  /api/v1/keys {name (required), limit (daily USD cap), provisioning (bool)} ->
  {data:KeyResource, key:"xpl_..."} (plaintext exactly once); GET / PATCH
  ({name, disabled, limit}; disabled:true revokes, terminal) / DELETE
  /api/v1/keys/{hash} where {hash} is the key's hash field (its uuid id), never
  the secret. On list/CRUD resources usage and limit_remaining are null today
  (real per-key spend: GET /api/v1/key or /api/v1/usage?api_key_id=).
- Key-per-customer is the alternative to safety_identifier attribution:
  independent revocation and per-customer daily caps; the two combine.
- Identities (spend buckets, one per team or purpose) are set up with the
  same provisioning key, the routes an org admin would otherwise click through
  on https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/api-keys. What that key can call: GET /api/whoami; GET, POST /api/orgs/{org_id}/identities; PATCH /api/orgs/{org_id}/identities/{identity_id} (display_name and description only); GET, POST /api/v1/keys; GET, PATCH, DELETE /api/v1/keys/{hash}; GET, PUT /api/orgs/{org_id}/budgets; DELETE /api/orgs/{org_id}/budgets/{budget_id} (identity- and key-scope budgets this key created); GET /api/orgs/{org_id}/usage/by-identity.
  POST identities takes {display_name, identity_id?, description?}; identity_id
