   REPLACE URL variables such as OPENROUTER_BASE_URL with it. An Anthropic SDK
   appends /v1/messages itself: its base is the bare origin https://api.experientiallabs.ai
   (never .../v1, which doubles to /v1/v1/messages). Do NOT
   delete OPENROUTER_API_KEY or the OpenRouter key from .env, secret stores or
   CI: stop reading it, leave it in place; I revoke it at openrouter.ai/keys.
   A key COMMITTED in a config file (ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN in a checked-in
   .claude/settings.json) is already leaked: remove it there, never send it on.
   Coding agents: Claude Code uses ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://api.experientiallabs.ai"
   (no /v1); the key rides ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (never ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN) via
   a shell export, the gitignored .claude/settings.local.json, or an
   apiKeyHelper reading .env, never the committed .claude/settings.json; remap
   EVERY model variable (ANTHROPIC_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL,
   ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL) to slugs or a background role keeps calling an
   expensive model. OpenCode, Cline, Continue, Cursor and Codex take the
   OpenAI base https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1.

3. Map model ids. Call GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/v1/models with my
   key (free, spends no credits). EVERY entry carries canonical_slug, the
   plain slug the gateway serves; ids are usually vendor/slug (vendor/slug:free
   for a free lane), sometimes a bare slug (gpt-6-astra, grok-4); ~vendor/x-latest
   ids are rolling aliases, for projects that used OpenRouter's :latest ids.
   For each OpenRouter id from step 1: strip any :nitro, :floor, :online,
   :thinking, :extended, :beta or :exacto suffix (those variants do not exist
   here; only :free does), then match canonical_slug == the part after the
   vendor's slash (openai/gpt-6-astra -> gpt-6-astra, anthropic/claude-sonnet-5
   -> claude-sonnet-5, deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash -> deepseek-v4-flash).
   No match: look for the same model under a slightly different spelling and
   use ONE obvious candidate, noted in the report. openrouter/auto and every
   id still unmapped: ask me one question listing each with your best
   candidates from the list, then wait. Never guess a model I did not pick.
   Use canonical_slug EXACTLY as returned; a vendor/slug id works verbatim
   ONLY when it is in the list (x-ai/grok-4 for the bare grok-4 answers 403
   model_not_granted: that means "use the canonical_slug", not an entitlement
   problem). LiteLLM: model "openai/<slug>" (replace the "openrouter/" prefix)
   with api_base https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/v1 and api_key from the new var.

4. Keep the request shapes (OpenAI Chat Completions and Responses bodies, SSE
   streaming, tool calling, json_schema, response shapes). Strip EVERY
   OpenRouter-only field BEFORE the first call: each one left in is either
   silently ignored or its own 400 unsupported_parameter naming it in "param".
   - usage: {"include": true} (a guaranteed 400 today); for a stream send
     stream_options: {"include_usage": true} instead (non-streams carry usage).
   - provider (order, allow_fallbacks, ignore, quantizations, sort, ...):
     accepted and silently ignored (not disclosed); the gateway routes and
     fails over itself. The one honored key is "provider": {"zdr": true}, a
     per-request zero-data-retention demand; keep exactly that if I used it.
   - transforms, route, models (fallback list: use its first model), plugins.
   - HTTP-Referer / X-Title headers: harmless, not shown; attribute via safety_identifier.
   Vercel AI SDK: replace @openrouter/ai-sdk-provider with @ai-sdk/openai
   (createOpenAI({ baseURL, apiKey })) or @ai-sdk/openai-compatible.
   "reasoning": {"effort"} is translated to reasoning_effort (rewriting it is optional).
   Unsupported efforts may only move down if policy permits and the request is admissible; else 400.
   "none" means off and can be refused; "minimal" still enables reasoning.
   On non-reasoning routes, effort may drop only when policy permits and the request is admissible.
   Translated, dropped or adjusted fields are usually listed in the reply's
   x-experiential-ignored-parameters JSON body field (not a header): informational.
   Anthropic-shaped traffic through OpenRouter (an Anthropic SDK, Claude Code)
   moves to the native Messages API, POST https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/v1/messages
   (SDK base: the bare origin, step 2), same key; no Idempotency-Key there.
   Responses API previous_response_id: continuation resolves ONLY while my
   org's capture_prompt_content is on and within the retention window; with
   capture off the second turn 400s previous_response_not_found. If the
   project chains turns that way, read
     GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/orgs/<org_id>/telemetry-settings (org_id: /api/whoami);
   if off, ask me ONE question: turn it on (PUT the same route,
   {"capture_prompt_content": true}; it stores my prompts with Experiential)
   or rewrite the chain to resend the full conversation each turn.

5. Move cost reads. Every chat / responses reply carries usage.cost (USD, what
   I was charged) and usage.is_byok; on a stream it rides the final usage
   chunk (step 4's stream_options). A request sent with Idempotency-Key
   carries no usage.cost at all, so read the field as optional. Same key on
   all of these, under https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/v1:
     GET /generation?id=<the x-request-id response header>   one request
     GET /usage     settled per-request rows (api_key_id, cost) for billing
     GET /credits   balance      GET /key   key info (OpenRouter's /auth/key)
     GET /activity  per-day rollup (not per request)
   OpenRouter's /models/user has no equivalent: use /models. /usage is paginated
   (50 rows + next_cursor) and, like /activity, ORG-wide: filter ?api_key_id=<my
   key's id, on every row> and match my x-request-id, or use /generation?id=.

6. My own provider keys (BYOK). If step 1 found provider keys I routed through
   OpenRouter (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GEMINI, XAI, DEEPSEEK, AZURE,
   AWS/Bedrock, Fireworks, ...), ask whether to connect them with no markup:
     GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/whoami   -> org_id
     GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/orgs/<org_id>/provider-connections
   List existing accounts FIRST. For EACH new account, ask me for a unique
   setup_alias (1-63 lowercase letters, digits, hyphens or underscores), unused
   across all providers in my org; multiple keys need distinct account names.
     POST https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/orgs/<org_id>/provider-connections/<provider>
         Content-Type: application/json
         {"setup_alias": "<unique-account-name>", "secret": "<that provider key>"}
   Never overwrite an existing account. On 409 account_exists choose another
   name and retry POST, never bypass it with PUT. PUT is only for a deliberate
   rotation I request, with that saved account's exact setup_alias and config.
   Provider: openai, anthropic, gemini, xai, deepseek, or any other whose
   credential is ONE string; never my OpenRouter key: I am leaving OpenRouter.
   azure_openai, bedrock, fireworks, vertex and modal need structured config
   or a token pair: connect those at
   https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/settings/connections instead.
   Use INFERENCE keys, never admin keys, as secret; OpenAI/Anthropic admin keys
   belong only in optional spend_secret. If spend_error is present,
   the serving key WAS saved: report partial success, never repeat POST; retry
   only the SAME returned connection.setup_alias with PUT, retaining its serving
   secret and config. Read check.status; if not "valid", tell me
   check.status_detail.remediation and stop. A 402 pro_required means a FIRST connection needs Pro
   (https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/credits); an org already holding one keeps connecting.
   Saving keys adds no arbitrary models: let me select each account on the
   chosen catalog model's waterfall with Use this account. Never echo a key.

7. Verify. Make ONE minimal call (model + messages, a small max_tokens) with
   the CHEAPEST mapped slug: a reasoning model can cost cents even for a
   smoke, and an empty pricing object in the listing means unknown: read
   GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/models/<slug>, and if that 404s (an alias)
   price the model it resolves to (its canonical_slug) or skip it and smoke a
   priced slug. Stream if the project streams (add stream_options:
   {"include_usage": true} so the final chunk carries usage.cost); if the
   project chains previous_response_id, verify a TWO-turn continuation, not a
   single call. Report the model, that it succeeded, and its usage.cost, or
   read the cost from GET /api/v1/generation?id=<x-request-id>, which works
   either way; then confirm the request's row on GET /api/v1/usage by that
   x-request-id (I can also see it at https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/logs). On a credits
   or activation error, tell me to finish activation at https://platform.experientiallabs.ai
   and stop; do not retry against OpenRouter. Then run the project's tests.

8. Report back: every file changed; the model-id mapping and the ids I still
   need to decide; the OpenRouter-only fields removed; where EXPLABS_API_KEY
   lives; that the OpenRouter key stays in place for me to revoke; the
   verification result. Full contract: https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/llms.txt; human
   docs: https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/docs/integrate.

### Switch from Cloudflare AI Gateway
Assess rules, customer plans, model-group allowances, BYOK and custom providers before moving traffic. The agent asks before writes, spend, privacy changes or cutover, and stops on unsupported requirements or missing live proof.

Help me assess and then migrate this project's Cloudflare AI Gateway traffic
onto the Experiential Labs gateway. Start with a read-only inventory and a
proposed mapping. This prompt is NOT blanket consent: ask for my explicit
approval before any file or policy writes, credential storage or rotation,
paid probes or other spend, traffic cutover, privacy/retention changes, or
secret revocation. Explain each proposed change and its rollback first.
My Experiential key is: xpl_...
If it is still "xpl_...", ask me for a key or direct me to
https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/api-keys. Do not assume an inference key has admin authority.
Never print secrets, put them in committed files, or send an Experiential key
to Cloudflare or an upstream provider. Redact secret values in every report.

1. Inventory before editing. Find Cloudflare AI Gateway URLs (including
   gateway.ai.cloudflare.com, provider-specific paths, /compat and custom-*
   providers), SDKs, fetch/curl clients, Workers bindings, env variables, CI
   and secret-store references. List call sites, endpoints and model ids.
   Identify Chat Completions, Responses, Messages, streaming, tool calls,
   structured output, continuation, batches and any other used API surface.
   Record Cloudflare headers such as cf-aig-authorization, cf-aig-metadata,
   cf-aig-cache-ttl, cf-aig-skip-cache, cf-aig-custom-cost and cf-aig-log-level,
   plus all other cf-aig-* headers, retry/fallback settings and timeouts.
   Separate Cloudflare gateway/admin tokens from direct OpenAI/Anthropic or
   other provider inference credentials. A Cloudflare token is not BYOK for
   those providers. Inspect references without exposing secret values.

2. Ask for the actual Cloudflare rule export and customer subscription rules.
   Record dynamic-routing conditions, rule order, rate/spend limits, metadata
   filters/split dimensions and provider/model overrides. Identify the trusted
   customer id and the server-side subscription source. Cloudflare custom
   metadata labels are NOT authentication or authorization. Neither request
   metadata.plan, user nor safety_identifier may select a customer's plan.
   The application server must map its authenticated customer to an Experiential
   identity; all that identity's keys, including rotated keys, share policy.
   Inventory each tier's allowed models, Basic/Frontier (or other) model groups,
   exact memberships, separate allowance amounts, currency and cost basis.
   These are my authored groups, not universal model classes or platform
   Free/Pro subscriptions. Never turn illustrative amounts into defaults.
   Ask about reset timezone and window (fixed, rolling, billing-anniversary or
   UTC calendar-month), carryover, current-period usage and pending requests,
   carry-in at cutover, upgrades/downgrades and over-limit behavior. A zero
   allowance means hard zero, not unlimited. Also inventory the shared total
   across all groups and the exact action on group exhaustion. An absent/null
   aggregate_limit_nano_usd means no shared cap; zero denies. on_exhausted
   defaults to deny; next_model requires explicit policy and a certified
   server-authored model chain, never an arbitrary client retry. Aggregate
   exhaustion and forbidden models still stop. Unknown plans must block mapping,
   never become unassigned identities. Do not silently reset usage.

3. Read THIS deployment's live contract and catalog before proposing APIs:
     https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/llms.txt
     https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/docs/integrate
     https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/docs/account-api
     https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/docs/cost-api
     GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/whoami
     GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1/models
     GET https://api.experientiallabs.ai/api/v1/models
   Use the catalog's canonical_slug and verified alias resolution to map every
   model, including provider-prefixed ids and custom models. Do not simply strip
   a prefix, assume a model exists, or replace one without asking me. Catalog
   discovery is not proof of this customer's access or successful serving.
   Build a requirement table: existing behavior, proposed mapping, live-doc
   evidence, test needed and blocker. Discover exact native model-group,
   customer-plan, assignment and allowance API routes from live documentation;
   do not invent routes, fields, or claim these controls are already deployed.
   Require native identity-bound access and separate per-group allowances,
   not application-side checks dressed up as equivalent gateway enforcement.
   Confirm admin/delegated assignment authority separately from provisioning
   keys and inference keys. Customers must not change plans, mint escape keys,
   or read another identity's usage; caller-supplied filters are not isolation.
   Verify allowed-model access across public models, aliases, retries/fallback
   and every used serving surface; unsupported lanes must refuse plan keys.
   Verify shared counters across keys, settled usage plus pending reservations,
   pricing revisions, plan-change effective times and preserved spent amounts.
   Read whoami's identity_id, customer_plan_identity_id and is_provisioning;
   restricted keys may self-read it, but that does not grant management rights.
   The implemented period contract supports UTC calendar-month or an explicit
   authoritative source interval with source_period_id and timezone-aware start/end.
   Explicit periods expire without automatic renewal; omitted budget_period on
   a plan change preserves it. Rolling windows are unsupported. Never rename,
   overlap or backdate a used source period to refill it. Treat unsupported
   reset/carryover rules as blockers, not approximations. Discover the documented
   allowance-cutover contract too, without assuming THIS deployment has it.
   If documented carry-in is unavailable, ask about a deliberate next-period cutover;
   never silently grant a fresh full allowance.

4. Map provider and cost behavior, not just a base URL. Existing Account API
   provisioning and Cost API settled exports are useful but do not by themselves
   prove subscription-policy parity. Keep wallet charges separate from customer
   allowance attribution. BYOK must not debit platform credits; attributed BYOK
   inference value uses a frozen rate schedule and is an estimate, NOT a provider
   invoice. Inventory input/output, cache-read/write, reasoning, long-context
   and custom rates, billable failures, missing usage and pending exposure.
   Unknown prices or missing usage must not turn a monetary allowance into free
   requests. Verify the allowance API reads the counters enforcement uses.
   Subscription events and invoicing stay in my application. For external
   billing, poll the documented settled Cost API export with pagination,
   durable checkpoints and deduplication; reconcile request ids, late settlement
   and retries. Do not invent webhooks or bill from a daily rollup or wallet
   balance. Treat inline usage.cost as optional; do not confuse it with a BYOK
   allowance estimate. Verify reporting scopes with two customer identities.
   List existing provider accounts before proposing BYOK. Ask before saving
   anything; use a distinct setup_alias for each new account and create-only
   POST from the live contract, never PUT over an existing account. Rotation
   needs separate approval. Respect the live plan entitlement for new BYOK
   connections; saving a provider key does not add arbitrary model support.

5. Custom providers need their own proof. Cloudflare custom providers can use
   arbitrary HTTP paths and native bodies; Experiential's supported adapters
   and model-bound custom endpoints are NOT an arbitrary HTTP proxy. Inventory
   the exact URL, wire protocol, auth headers, model ids, usage format and rate
   units. Use the documented Vault-backed connection/custom-endpoint flow and
   its validation, not a new proxy or a made-up Cloudflare provider connection.
   Custom endpoint rates are not inferred from public provider prices. Confirm
   the live rate_card contract, full schedule and frozen revision. Without an
   authored card, custom pricing is unknown, not free. New custom accounts need
   an explicit unique setup_alias and create-only POST. For key or rate changes,
   create a new custom account and deliberately select Use on the model; do not
   rotate it through the generic provider PUT or probe at the official origin.
   For Tinfoil (TinFoil), verify the endpoint and SDK's enclave-attestation and
   privacy requirements. OpenAI compatibility does NOT prove attestation survives
   an intermediary. If the required guarantee cannot be verified, stop that move.
   Keep Modal separate from the Cloudflare transfer. Determine whether it uses
   Modal proxy authentication, an application bearer, or another supported scheme,
   and whether it bills tokens or time/GPU usage. Do not claim token-cost parity
   for unsupported billing units. Name any adapter, auth, usage or pricing gap
   as a blocker and scope it separately; never silently reroute these services.

6. Preserve privacy and runtime semantics. Inventory prompt/response logging,
   retention, zero-data-retention/no-training needs, cache keys/TTL/bypass,
   cache hits and their accounting, retries, fallback order and timeout budgets.
   Cloudflare response caching is not the same as provider prompt caching.
   Map each cf-aig-* header to a documented control or report it unsupported;
   never forward Cloudflare auth to the new host or silently drop a required rule.
   Check continuation requirements such as previous_response_id against the live
   capture_prompt_content contract. Ask before enabling storage; offer resending
   the full conversation where supported instead. Never weaken privacy to make
   a smoke pass. Check retry/idempotency behavior per API surface, including
   ambiguous disconnects; do not assume every retry is free or safe to replay.

7. Present the mapping and blockers, then wait for approval of specific edits.
   For supported OpenAI clients the base is https://api.experientiallabs.ai/v1 with
   Authorization: Bearer $EXPLABS_API_KEY. An Anthropic SDK appends /v1/messages
   itself: use the bare origin https://api.experientiallabs.ai, not a doubled /v1 base.
   Store keys only in the approved local env/secret scheme, never source control.
   Preserve unrelated Cloudflare DNS, Workers, Turnstile and other services.
   Keep old untracked .env secrets, CI secrets and Cloudflare/provider tokens
   in place for rollback until deliberate revocation is approved. A committed
   secret is exposed: flag it and ask for removal/rotation, never echo it.
   Propose a reversible configuration diff and keep a redacted baseline of
   endpoint, model and policy settings. Do not switch production traffic yet.

8. Ask for an isolated test environment, bounded credentials and a request/spend
   budget before probes; connection checks may themselves make paid calls.
   Pin platform revision, deployed engine versions, schema, configuration and
   catalog/pricing revisions. Run local tests first; label mocks as mocks.
   With approval, test actual providers and the project's real request shapes,
   streams/tools/continuations, two customers, multiple models per group,
   independent allowance depletion, forbidden-model refusal before dispatch,
   key rotation, concurrent reservations, retries/fallback, interrupted streams,
   reset/plan changes, shared aggregate depletion, deny versus next_model,
   identity-scoped reports and BYOK without wallet debits. Reconcile request ids,
   settled costs and native plus imported pending allowance exposure. A single
   successful completion does not establish policy, billing or privacy parity.
   Stop before cutover on unsupported requirements or absent live verification.
   Do not autoactivate production policy or move traffic. Only after evidence and
   a separate cutover approval, use the supported administrator handoff:
   - Prepare at most 500 immutable, disjoint source-owned per-request receipts,
     each with external_ref, frozen group reference, settled and pending amounts.
     Never import cumulative snapshots or requests already counted by the destination.
     Pin exact period, source watermark, coverage and evidence digest. Identical
     prepare retries are idempotent; changed replays/overlapping exports refuse.
     More than 500 receipts is a blocker for this bounded path, not permission
     to truncate, aggregate them or invent pagination.
   - Prepare closes that identity's destination admission even while global
     enforcement is inactive. It does not stop Cloudflare. Explicitly stop source
     dispatch and reconcile in-flight ownership before activating with source_frozen
     and independent source-stop evidence. This is NOT a transaction across gateways.
     Require the documented trusted administrator transport; an ordinary or delegated
     provisioning key cannot perform cutover. Do not invent a browser proxy or
     supply actor headers if the live contract does not provide an admin entrypoint.
   - Rollback must account for usage on BOTH gateways. Freeze destination admission,
     drain native reservations and resolve native pending plus all imported pending
     while active or frozen, then obtain a complete fresh export before acknowledgment.
     Any unresolved native or imported exposure blocks acknowledgment.
     Include settled_periods across all historical periods, not just the current one.
     Preserve the original JSON and parse/serialize money losslessly with Python
     integers/exact decimals or a JavaScript lossless BigInt JSON library. Totals
     can exceed 2^53 - 1. Never use ordinary JSON.parse, response.json() or Number
     for rollback amounts; rounding cannot be repaired afterward. Send exact JSON
     integers, not numeric strings, and return the server-issued digest unchanged.
     The export bounds are 500 native outstanding rows, 500 external receipts and
     1,000 settled-period rows; overflow is never proof of a complete export.
     A changed export_sha256 or export_overflow blocks acknowledgment. Rolled-back
     destination admission stays closed; no step resets history or releases unknown
     usage. Unresolved prior exposure or destination use in the same period blocks
     a new prepare. Never grant extra allowance or replay uncertain paid requests.
   Keep old secrets until I deliberately approve revocation after verification.

9. Report pass/fail/blocked/untested for every requirement, changed files, model
   mappings, policy/reset/carry-in decisions, credential locations (no values),
   tests and their pinned cutoff, billing reconciliation and rollback steps.
   Distinguish existing Account/Cost APIs, new native controls and their actual
   deployment status, application billing work and unverified provider behavior.
   Never claim full Cloudflare parity before this workflow is tested.

## Web app URL map (where to send a human)

  https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/                     sign in, then land on your key and credits
  https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/models               the catalog: search, detail, compare
  https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/playground           chat with any model in the browser
  https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/settings/api-keys    mint and revoke API Keys
  https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/settings             connect BYOK provider keys
  https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/settings/data-controls  Data controls: the zero-data-retention switch, the
                              prompt/response storage switch, routing requirements
                              (require_zdr, require_no_training), processing regions
                              and the provider posture reference
  https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/credits              balance, spend, and adding credits
  https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/spend                financial reporting by model, key, prompt and tags
  https://platform.experientiallabs.ai/logs                 request/attempt activity and captured-content inspection
